entities.summary:
Neoptolemus II of Epirus: King of Epirus from 302 BC until his death

As the son of King Alexander I of Epirus and Cleopatra of Macedonia, Neoptolemus II ascended to the throne at a young age, inheriting a complex web of alliances and rivalries between ancient Macedon and Epirus. His reign was marked by a series of strategic marriages and military campaigns aimed at consolidating his power and securing Epirus's position amidst the rivalries of ancient Greece.

Despite his efforts, Neoptolemus II's reign was cut short by a series of devastating wars with neighboring states, including the Phocians and the Athenians. His death in 296 BCE marked the end of an era for Epirus, and his legacy would be shaped by the tumultuous events of the Hellenistic period.

The impact of Neoptolemus II's reign can still be felt today, with his strategic marriages and alliances playing a significant role in the formation of the Hellenistic kingdoms of the Mediterranean.

A striking testament to the enduring power of ancient Greek diplomacy is the inscription on the tomb of Neoptolemus II, which reads: 'I, Neoptolemus, King of Epirus, have done what was just and good.'
